queue-audit-residue-miscited-as-preexist.reason: Re-read the bullet at 9c03a19a7480548cac5aad7fa9fa53405cb2fe2c. It now retracts the earlier claim in terms, says plainly that it was wrong for three of the five, gives the per-row table (Crate 1431 to 1427, Coin 1148 to 1147, daGmch_c 1119 to 1120) with each row delta matched to its source-file line delta, and keeps only ChiefChilly and Player as pre-existing -- which the base control independently confirms are exactly the two rows main is red on. ONE RESIDUAL IMPRECISION, settled here as clearing without a new finding. The bullet attributes the ChiefChilly/Player staleness to main's 9b8cb8add editing include/ChiefChilly.h and include/Player.h. That is the wrong half of the commit: queue_audit derives total_lines by summing lines over the delinks-resolved source paths of the row's range, which are src/ paths only, and no include/ path appears in config/arm9/delinks.txt, so a header edit cannot move the cell. The same commit 9b8cb8add also edited src/_ZN11ChiefChillyD1Ev.cpp and src/_ZN6PlayerD1Ev.cpp, and those are what moved the numbers: measured with git show 9b8cb8add^:<path> piped to wc -l against git show 9b8cb8add:<path>, 22 to 23 and 35 to 36, which are exactly the +1 deltas the two rows need. The commit attribution and the direction of responsibility are therefore both correct and independently verified; 9b8cb8add is an ancestor of both bdcb1df7d and the branch's merge-base c52f63ca5, so it is genuinely main's. Only the named mechanism is wrong. It moves no number, changes no gate verdict and does not affect this branch's attribution, and under source_review a provenance finding may not be deferred, so raising it would require a corrective commit that mode verify forbids -- converting a wrong noun into a hard publish refusal. It clears as-is and is recorded here so the next writer touching this bullet fixes the sentence. Disposition unchanged: fixed.

dead-references-koopa-plus-truncation.reason: Every element reproduced independently on the MERGE TREE at 0befb1b8f5d4c832f7ab23ff9478c12f7e4f54b0. (1) python tools/check_dead_references.py exits 0 on the merge tree and 0 on the base control, exit codes captured directly to files and never through a pipe. (2) The branch-level diff of config/dead-reference-baseline.json adds exactly ONE entry -- file notes/agents/handoffs/issue-2411-humanizer-2.md, ref src_tu/actors/Koopa -- and removes none. (3) The tool was not weakened: the branch-level git diff over tools/ is entirely EMPTY, so check_dead_references.py is byte-identical to main's. (5) The precedent is real: the baseline already carries (notes/actor-leaf-provenance.md, src_tu/actors/EnemySpawner), the identical truncation of src_tu/actors/EnemySpawner+EnemySwitchTag.cpp. RESIDUAL IMPRECISION, disclosed rather than raised as a separate finding: the handoff and the verifier's own reason call that precedent one entry above the new pair; the file sorts by (file, ref) and the precedent is at index 1 while the new entry is at index 12, so it is eleven entries above, not one. queue-audit-residue-miscited-as-preexist.reason: Re-read the bullet at 9c03a19a7480548cac5aad7fa9fa53405cb2fe2c. It now retracts the earlier claim in terms, says plainly that it was wrong for three of the five, gives the per-row table (Crate 1431 to 1427, Coin 1148 to 1147, daGmch_c 1119 to 1120) with each row delta matched to its source-file line delta, and keeps only ChiefChilly and Player as pre-existing -- which the base control independently confirms are exactly the two rows main is red on. ONE RESIDUAL IMPRECISION, settled here as clearing without a new finding. The bullet attributes the ChiefChilly/Player staleness to main's 9b8cb8add editing include/ChiefChilly.h and include/Player.h. That is the wrong half of the commit: queue_audit derives total_lines by summing lines over the delinks-resolved source paths of the row's range, which are src/ paths only, and no include/ path appears in config/arm9/delinks.txt, so a header edit cannot move the cell. The same commit 9b8cb8add also edited src/_ZN11ChiefChillyD1Ev.cpp and src/_ZN6PlayerD1Ev.cpp, and those are what moved the numbers: measured with git show 9b8cb8add^:<path> piped to wc -l against git show 9b8cb8add:<path>, 22 to 23 and 35 to 36, which are exactly the +1 deltas the two rows need. The commit attribution and the direction of responsibility are therefore both correct and independently verified; 9b8cb8add is an ancestor of both bdcb1df7d and the branch's merge-base c52f63ca5, so it is genuinely main's. Only the named mechanism is wrong. It moves no number, changes no gate verdict and does not affect this branch's attribution, and under source_review a provenance finding may not be deferred, so raising it would require a corrective commit that mode verify forbids -- converting a wrong noun into a hard publish refusal. It clears as-is and is recorded here so the next writer touching this bullet fixes the sentence. Disposition unchanged: fixed.
queue-audit-residue-miscited-as-preexist.summary: The handoff attributed all five stale queue rows to main; three were the branch's own.

The bullet attributes the ChiefChilly/Player staleness to main's 9b8cb8add editing include/ChiefChilly.h and include/Player.h. That is the wrong half of the commit: queue_audit derives total_lines by summing lines over the delinks-resolved source paths of the row's range, which are src/ paths only, and no include/ path appears in config/arm9/delinks.txt, so a header edit cannot move the cell. The same commit 9b8cb8add also edited src/_ZN11ChiefChillyD1Ev.cpp and src/_ZN6PlayerD1Ev.cpp, and those are what moved the numbers: measured with git show 9b8cb8add^:<path> piped to wc -l against git show 9b8cb8add:<path>, 22 to 23 and 35 to 36, which are exactly the +1 deltas the two rows need. The commit attribution and the direction of responsibility are therefore both correct and independently verified; 9b8cb8add is an ancestor of both bdcb1df7d and the branch's merge-base c52f63ca5, so it is genuinely main's. Only the named mechanism is wrong. It moves no number, changes no gate verdict and does not affect this branch's attribution, and under source_review a provenance finding may not be deferred, so raising it would require a corrective commit that mode verify forbids -- converting a wrong noun into a hard publish refusal. It clears as-is and is recorded here so the next writer touching this bullet fixes the sentence. Disposition unchanged: fixed.

It now retracts the earlier claim in terms, says plainly that it was wrong for three of the five, gives the per-row table (Crate 1431 to 1427, Coin 1148 to 1147, daGmch_c 1119 to 1120) with each row delta matched to its source-file line delta, and keeps only ChiefChilly and Player as pre-existing -- which the base control independently confirms are exactly the two rows main is red on. The bullet attributes the ChiefChilly/Player staleness to main's 9b8cb8add editing include/ChiefChilly.h and include/Player.h. That is the wrong half of the commit: queue_audit derives total_lines by summing lines over the delinks-resolved source paths of the row's range, which are src/ paths only, and no include/ path appears in config/arm9/delinks.txt, so a header edit cannot move the cell. The same commit 9b8cb8add also edited src/_ZN11ChiefChillyD1Ev.cpp and src/_ZN6PlayerD1Ev.cpp, and those are what moved the numbers: measured with git show 9b8cb8add^:<path> piped to wc -l against git show 9b8cb8add:<path>, 22 to 23 and 35 to 36, which are exactly the +1 deltas the two rows need. The commit attribution and the direction of responsibility are therefore both correct and independently verified; 9b8cb8add is an ancestor of both bdcb1df7d and the branch's merge-base c52f63ca5, so it is genuinely main's. Only the named mechanism is wrong. It moves no number, changes no gate verdict and does not affect this branch's attribution, and under source_review a provenance finding may not be deferred, so raising it would require a corrective commit that mode verify forbids -- converting a wrong noun into a hard publish refusal.     daPropeller_Heyho_Fire_c: name the fireball's fields and drop the views
    
    The five helpers take a typed daPropeller_Heyho_Fire_c * (func_ov002_020fed7c
    keeps the char * that include/decl_common.h declares and casts inside) and
    read members by name: otherOwner and hitFlags on the hit cylinder, the
    Player's mIsVanish and mIsMetal, mCamSpacePos, mPrevAngleY and the speeds.
    FindWithID, SmallPoofDust, MarkForDestruction, IsOnGround, IsOnWall,
    Sound::Play, Model::LoadFile and ModelBase::SetFile are called through their
    headers instead of mangled externs. Render calls mModel.Render(0) instead of
    a local Base/Derived vtable view (the call stays virtual), and the C/PMF
    view of the state is gone: State now declares its init handler at 0x00, and
    the slot at 0x354 is named mTurnedBack. The banner and comments describe the
    one state (init func_ov002_020fed18, main func_ov002_020fec94, read from the
    ROM relocs at 0x0210d600/0x0210d5f8).
    
    Measured negatives, kept with a comment: dropping the isPlayer temp shrinks
    func_ov002_020feb50 0x144 -> 0x138; a plain s16 mStateTimer read is an
    ldrsh where the ROM has ldrh; dCcAc_c::Init through the header with a
    Fix12<int> local grows InitResources 0xd8 -> 0xec and adds a .rodata word.
    
    Proof: the object before and after is identical (every section's bytes,
    relocations by offset/type/symbol, defined and undefined symbol sets).
    tubuild verify 14/14 MATCH TEXT-VERIFIED; linkcheck SCRATCH-DATA-VERIFIED.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

    Heyho fireball, daBtn_c: correct the review's prose and measurement findings
    
    Review fixes for the two readability commits before this one. No emitted
    byte or relocation destination changes.
    
    daPropeller_Heyho_Fire_c
    - The metal-player branch does not "turn the fireball round". It flips
      mPrevAngleY half a turn and zeroes unk_0a4/unk_0ac, the x and z of the
      velocity dActor_c::UpdatePosWithOnlySpeed adds. Then it sets mVertSpeed
      0x1e000 and mVertAccel -0x4000. The banner and the inline comment now
      say that: the facing flips, horizontal motion stops, and the fireball
      launches upward.
    - The header field mTurnedBack (0x354) becomes mDeflected: set when a
      metal player deflected it; func_ov002_020fec94 then skips the
      player-hit test. Only this file uses the header (tools/affected_src.py).
    - The hitFlags 0x10 note now cites dCc_c.h's unverified best-effort table.
    - The dCcAc_c::Init limit names the spellings measured:
      `Fix12<int> r = { 0xa000 };` passed twice gives 0xd8 -> 0xec plus a
      .rodata word; `r.val = 0xa000;` gives 0xe4 and no .rodata.
    
    daBtn_c
    - Sound::LoadAndSetMusic_Layer3 / StopLoadedMusic_Layer3 are no longer
      mangled externs. A local `namespace Sound` declaration outside the
      extern "C" block works, the same form daKuriKing_c.cpp uses. The three
      call sites use it, and the banner's "Known limits" entry for them is
      gone. The new prototypes have no named parameters, like the old ones,
      so the @NNN count holds.
    - The previous commit message and the @NNN comment said sixteen
      prototypes were retired. It was nineteen, and -33 is their named
      parameters. The comment now says so. The +30 from Message.h and
      dCamera_c.h together stands; the review measured them at +16 and +14
      alone. The source gives no per-include numbers.
    - Behavior's timer: the reset is now `mStateTimer = 0`. The comment says
      spelling both statements through mStateTimer changes the code (either
      one alone does not), and so does `mStateTimer++`.
    - func_ov079_02123804: a plain mState read at either site gives
      0x288 -> 0x284; plain reads at both sites give 0x280 (re-measured).
    - func_ov079_02125058: volatile keeps v2's reloads as well as the stores.
    - The camera store comment says only what the code shows.
    - daBtn_c.h mTrackStarID: TrackStar also returns -1 for type 2 when the
      star is not the mission's STAR_ID (data_0209f220) and the current
      sublevel maps to level <= 0xe (dActor_c.cpp TrackStar).
    
    daWater_Hakidasi_c.h: its State comment no longer claims the same shape
    as Heyho's State, which now declares an int-returning mInit at 0x00.
    Comment only; its one consumer, src/actors/daWater_Hakidasi_c.cpp, compiles

The real, measured barrier is the one src/actors/Scuttlebug.cpp:196 states - 'Natural `new` selects the wrong allocator': the cartridge's factory calls fBase_c::operator new (_ZN7fBase_cnwEj), and mwccarm rejects an in-class operator new (include/fBase_c.h:150, accurately cited), so `new daMip_c()` would link but emit a call to the WRONG callee. The conclusion (keep the literal seam) is right; the stated reason is not, and the handoff's claim that Scuttlebug 'records the same measurement' misstates what Scuttlebug records. The strongest control reproduces exactly: the pre-#2530 baseline carrying eight real orphans passes with exit 0 under the base tool and fails with exit 1 naming all eight under the candidate. classify_missing branch 2 is confirmed unreachable from --check by an instrumented probe that demonstrably CAN return the other answer (it records 8 branch-2 hits from --update on the same baseline). --update's code is byte-identical to the base. What fails is the new PROSE, in a commit whose own third purpose is to make this docstring tell the truth. The two most serious prose findings are NOT producer error: the coordinator's brief specified the false --update behaviour and the producer built to it faithfully (see notes[0]). report_orphans' 'Do NOT reach for --update' paragraph makes three factual assertions about --update; measured against the eight orphans that motivated the change, --update demands no --reason, writes no exceptions row, exits 0 and RAISES count, and the resulting baseline then passes --check. The clause 'move count downward -- which this ratchet then reports as a regression' is false in every case: this is a set ratchet, load_baseline's own comment records that nothing reads count back, and --update rewrites the baseline so the next --check compares current to current. For the other orphan class -- a genuine deletion, which the function admits it cannot distinguish -- the change is a diagnostic regression: the base tool printed the exact working remedy (python tools/tiers_ratchet.py --update --reason "<why>"), while the candidate opens with the flat assertion 'Nothing regressed: the readable code is still in the tree', forbids --update, and names config/converted-backslide-exceptions.jsonl without naming any command that can write it -- --update --reason is the only writer. Two module-docstring bullets left in place still describe --check emitting 'MOVED -- absorbed into ...' and 'GONE -- not a tracked source file any more' and demanding a --reason for a path that left the tree; after this commit --check emits ORPHANED for both and demands nothing, and why()'s MOVED arms are reachable only from --update. The remedy paragraph is also a measured loophole rather than the right call: --update with no arguments at all silently launders the exact defect the gate exists to catch. Tests are green (32 + 35, both invocation forms) and the end-to-end class is genuinely behavioural, but no test covers the orphan-plus-backslide path and none guards the unchanged --update behaviour the change relies on. No source, header, config or ROM surface is touched; two tools files only; no attribution surface involved.

Rewrite each identity onto <promoted_source>#<symbol>' paragraph and, twelve lines below, 'CONVERTED backslide: 2 banked file(s) no longer pass all 5 criteria / src/actors/Promoted.cpp#First / No raw offset arithmetic' for that same destination. source_review.summary: The design is right and the mechanics are right. The producer took the two-diagnostic structure, hoisted orphan_destination() so one fact decides what the reader is told, and split report_orphans() into a REWRITE class and a FIND OUT WHAT HAPPENED class. I tested that as a claim rather than reading the sentences: nothing in the destination-known section asserts a --reason refusal, a falling count, or a regression, and nothing in the destination-unknown section asserts 'Nothing regressed' or that --update absorbs it. VFY-2543-01, -02, -03 and -04 are retired as scoped. VFY-2543-07 is fixed -- an orphan-only exit now lists absorbed_clean, confirmed on a tree carrying an orphan and a genuine identity upgrade together. VFY-2543-08 is fixed -- the literal-set restatement tests are gone, orphan-plus-backslide is covered, and UpdateBehaviourPin actually runs --update. VFY-2543-09 is fixed with a durable claim I re-measured true (both enumerations return 9,089 files, symmetric difference empty). VFY-2543-06 is acknowledged accurately and is not asserted away. The printed `--update --reason` command works exactly as its paragraph says: exit 0, one attributed exceptions row, count down, follow-up --check green -- the documented escape hatch, not a new hole. Tests are 42 and 35, both exit 0 unpiped, and the suite is falsifiable: 11 of the 42 fail against attempt-1's tool while the three UpdateBehaviourPin tests pass against base, attempt 1 and attempt 2 -- the right result, and explained rather than assumed, because the `if args.update:` block is byte-identical at all three commits. TWO THINGS FAIL, both in the same family as the finding this commit was reworked for: a claim printed without being checked, and prose describing output the tool no longer produces. First, 'Nothing regressed. The readable code is still in the tree under the destination named above' is printed for every orphan whose manifest names a destination, with no test that the destination is tracked or that it passes. why() eighty lines above checks both. On the real manifest, 136 promoted entries name a destination and only 7 of those destinations are fully CONVERTED -- 129 are tracked but failing. A single --check run demonstrably prints 'Nothing regressed' and then reports that same destination as a CONVERTED backslide, and following the printed remedy banks a failing identity. The docstring's own :53-56 says the failing destination is the by-construction outcome; the eight #2530 orphans simply happened to point at clean ones. Second, module docstring :42-58 still tells the reader that a GONE path is reported as a MOVE and is or is not a backslide depending on the absorbing file's members. Measured across three gone-path shapes, --check prints neither 'MOVED -- absorbed into' nor 'GONE -- not a tracked source file any more'; structurally it cannot, because both --check and the plain report subtract orphans before why() is reached, leaving why()'s gone-path ladder reachable only from --update's refusal. It also contradicts :90-96 of the same docstring. That is VFY-2543-05 recurring one section up, and it is partly my fault: I scoped 05 to :93-100, the producer fixed exactly what I named, and I missed the identical text at :42-58. Two lesser items: the epilogue at :742-748 opens 'MOVED lines above are a TU promotion' under a guard that can only be satisfied when no MOVED line was printed (0 live instances), and the printed rewrite target '<promoted_source>#<symbol>' is unconditional while tu_promote.py:218 uses a bare dest for a single-function TU (0 such entries today). No src/, header, config or ROM surface is touched; config/converted-baseline.json and config/converted-backslide-exceptions.jsonl are byte-identical to the base; no attribution surface is involved.

With the destination tracked the state is 'converted' and the clash is named; with it untracked the state is 'unvouched', the detail is 'it is not a tracked source file', and the clash is silent. And the state is REACHABLE, not hypothetical: `git ls-files` omits a file that exists on disk but has not been `git add`ed (demonstrated in a throwaway repo), so during the very workflow that creates orphans -- delinks row edited, destination written, not yet staged -- the destination is enrolled-with-many-members AND untracked. WHY THIS IS A NOTE AND NOT A FAIL, by the same bar I have used for four rounds (a reader-facing claim false on live data at scale): it is 0-live twice over (0 of 9008 ownership keys untracked, 0 of 136 promoted destinations untracked, 0 of 651 carried symbols disagreeing -- two independently-zero conditions must coincide), and in that state the report tells the reader NOT to rewrite ('no rewrite target this tool can vouch for'), so the missing clash costs no actionable advice. source_review.summary: First source review of ov043/daObjKm1_Kurumajiku_c at this commit, derived independently of the byte-only pass of 2026-09-07; that pass was treated as hearsay and none of its numbers were carried forward. Producer session was prod-kuruma-0907; this reviewer is fleet-0907-vfy-kuruma-adopt-0909, a different session, and attribution.json preserves the original per-member authors across the fold (tangosdev for D1, D0, InitResources and classInit; lunavyqo for CleanupResources) rather than reassigning them to the promoter. FAKE SLOT INTERFACE: absent, and proved rather than assumed. src/game/actors/d_a_obj_km1_kurumajiku.cpp and include/daObjKm1_Kurumajiku_c.h contain no cast over `this`, no fabricated slot struct, no manual vtable indexing and no mNN offset member; a grep for that whole pattern family over the TU and both headers returns nothing. The positive proof is romdata_check: the class's emitted _ZTV21daObjKm1_Kurumajiku_c compares equal to the cartridge for the full 128 bytes, all 32 slots, with relocations resolved -- so every slot target is the ROM's target, not merely a load+blx of the right shape. Reading the two images by hand confirms the leaf vtable is word-identical to daObjKurumajiku_c's ov002 table at 0x02109320 except at slots 0, 3, 16 and 17, which are exactly the four the header declares; nothing is silently inherited and nothing extra is overridden. The base's slots 0 and 3 are 0x00000000 in the cartridge, which is the `= 0` the base header spells, and no .text byte gate can see that. NAME PROVENANCE: the class name is ROM-evidenced, not coined. _ZTS at ov043 0x02112350 holds the NUL-terminated '21daObjKm1_Kurumajiku_c' and the _ZTI record at 0x02112338 points its middle word at that address; the retired tree spelling RickshawBdw appears nowhere in the image. The _ZTI third word is 0x021092f8 = _ZTI17daObjKurumajiku_c, an __si_class_type_info with one base at subobject offset 0, so the intermediate base the header asserts is stated by the cartridge; the D1 literal pool at 0x02111440 corroborates it independently with three vptr words (0x0211238c, 0x02109320, 0x0210ae38). The base class name daObjKurumajiku_c is likewise ROM-evidenced from ov002 _ZTS at 0x02109304. Method spellings InitResources, CleanupResources, Behavior, Render and the classInit suffix are the tree's established reconstructions carried in symbols.txt, not names this change invents; the ROM preserves no mangled member names. Coined and disclosed, not disguised: the local struct names ResourceDescriptor and Km1KurumajikuProfile (the latter field-for-field identical to the adjacent sibling d_a_obj_km1_kuruma.cpp's Km1KurumaProfile, one of 6 sources using those field names) and, in the unchanged base header, the placeholder field name mMountedActorIds, which is labelled a placeholder in situ while its 0x320 offset and 4x4 width are the observed facts. ADDRESS-DERIVED PLACEHOLDERS: exactly three in the reviewed TU -- func_ov002_020b6c54, func_ov002_020b6ac8 and data_ov043_02112344 -- plus two prose mentions of func_ov002_ names in the base header. All three are the live spellings in config/arm9/overlays/ov002/symbols.txt and ov043/symbols.txt, all three are disclosed in comments naming the literal pool they were read from, and check_references confirms no reference in the change resolves to nothing. There are no unk_ members and no cast standing in for a type other than the deliberately opaque three-word ResourceDescriptor, whose extent is bounded by _ZTS starting at 0x02112350 and whose third word points at a 'CLPS' collision blob at 0x02111bc0 -- consistent with the comment, which correctly declines to guess its members. RELOCATED WORDS: every address the source names was resolved to a configured symbol by hand rather than trusted from a byte match -- 0x020b6c54 and 0x020b6ac8 to the ov002 helper placeholders, 0x02109320 and 0x0210ae38 to _ZTV17daObjKurumajiku_c and _ZTV10dBgActor_c, 0x020b6b38 and 0x020b6b10 to daObjKurumajiku_c's own Behavior and Render, and the two classInit BL words decoded to 0x02043444 = _ZN7fBase_cnwEj and 0x020eea50 = _ZN10dBgActor_cC2Ev, which is what the header's `operator new` and implicit-constructor account requires. The InitResources constant 0x88 is checked against the KM1_KURUMA profile at 0x02112438, whose id half really is 0x0088, one below this class's 0x0089. .DATA POINTER WORDS: the rename hazard is closed in-commit. The four member symbols and the vtable are renamed from the RickshawBdw spelling inside config/arm9/overlays/ov043/symbols.txt in the same commit as the source, symbols/actor_renames.tsv gains the five matching rows, check_rename_ledger agrees every mangled and vtable row with its module's symbols.txt, and romdata_check reports zero differing words for this source -- so no pointer word links as 0. delinks.txt collapses the five legacy entries into one entry over 0x021113fc..0x02111518 with no gap and no overlap against the ukishima and kuruma neighbours, and the manifest's tiling arithmetic (0x50+0x64+0x14+0x18+0x3c = 0x11c) is correct. The manifest is honest about what it does not claim: text-only route, the .data band left unclaimed, tu_map's count of 4 called out as a floor because its _Spawn factory rule labels nothing in this image, and sinit corroboration recorded as module-wide rather than narrowed. OBSERVATIONS THAT DO NOT RISE TO FINDINGS: three prose citations now name the retired coined spelling -- include/daObjKurumajiku_c.h line 25 ('_ZN11RickshawBdwD1Ev stores this class's vtable') and line 39 ('RickshawBdw_Spawn'), and src/game/actors/d_a_obj_km1_ukishima.cpp line 16 -- in an unchanged header and an unchanged neighbour that this commit's rename made stale. Each underlying claim was re-derived from the ROM in this session and holds, and each citation still resolves on a fresh clone through the symbols/actor_renames.tsv row this same commit adds, so the evidence chain is intact. Measured context: 90 distinct mangled tokens cited in comments tree-wide resolve to no symbols.txt entry, across 90 files and 134 occurrences (Tree, Scuttlebug, Bully, BigMovingIceBlock among them); this change contributes 2 of the 134 and introduces no new category of debt. Separately, config/converted-baseline.json still lists the four deleted one-function paths and does not yet list the promoted members; tiers_ratchet reads that transition through the manifest and passes with +8 gained, so it is an un-banked gain rather than a loss. Nothing in the six reviewed paths required a symbols.txt alias or bounding row, and nothing was made to consult symbols/actor_renames.tsv to satisfy a data gate.

source_review.summary: Independent integration-stage source review, authored in session fleet-0907-int-adopt-0909 and derived from the files themselves rather than inherited from the 2026-09-09 verifier. I read the whole reconstructed TU, both headers, the manifest, the ov043 symbols.txt and delinks.txt deltas, the appended actor_renames.tsv rows and both queue rows. WHAT THE SOURCE CLAIMS AND WHY IT HOLDS. src/game/actors/d_a_obj_km1_kurumajiku.cpp declares five members and defines three of them, leaving the D1/D0 pair to the inline empty destructor in include/daObjKm1_Kurumajiku_c.h, which is the documented way to get mwccarm 2004/b56 to emit D1 before D0 and no leaf D2; the file states this in its own comment rather than leaving it to be rediscovered. The functions are written in the reverse of ROM address order, which is what mwccarm's reverse-source-order .text emission requires, and the comment says so and says the build refuses the object otherwise. The claimed run 0x021113fc..0x02111518 is derived by address and tiles exactly: 0x50 + 0x64 + 0x14 + 0x18 + 0x3c = 0x11c, bounded below by d_a_obj_km1_ukishima.cpp and above by d_a_obj_km1_kuruma.cpp, and the delinks.txt delta shows the five legacy one-function entries collapsing into that single range, which is the arithmetic I checked rather than took on trust. The class name is not coined: the header records _ZTS at ov043 0x02112350 reading 21daObjKm1_Kurumajiku_c and the typeinfo middle word at 0x0211233c pointing at it, and the intermediate base daObjKurumajiku_c is stated both by _ZTI+8 = 0x021092f8 and by the three-vptr destructor pool, which is the ROM RTTI ruling applied correctly rather than an English coinage. The header declares exactly the four slots the ROM's leaf vtable differs at (0, 3, 16, 17) and explicitly refuses to redeclare slots 6 and 9 because those words are daObjKurumajiku_c's own ov002 Behavior and Render, so no override is silently inherited and none is fabricated. There is no fake slot interface, no unk_ member, no offset cast and no magic address dispatch anywhere in the TU. WHAT IS DISCLOSED RATHER THAN HIDDEN. func_ov002_020b6c54 and func_ov002_020b6ac8 are the tree's own existing symbols.txt names for those two ov002 addresses, not names this work invented, and the source says it read their identity off the literal pools at 0x021114d4 and 0x021114bc rather than from relocs.txt because relocated words are wildcards to the byte comparison. ResourceDescriptor is declared and not defined, so the entry claims .text only and guesses at no member it never dereferences; Km1KurumajikuProfile field names are coined and the source labels the coining, with the 0x1c size asserted at compile time. fBase_c::operator new is reached through an extern C alias of the mangled symbol, which is this tree's established convention and is required for correctness because a plain new relocates to the unavailable global operator new. INTEGRATION JUDGMENT. The change carries its own queue-row refresh: notes/data/tu-promotion-queue.tsv replaces the RickshawBdw row with a daObjKm1_Kurumajiku_c row and flips already_promoted from no to yes, and notes/data/class-build-worklist.tsv drops its alias annotation, so merging this does not by itself make the queue row stale. The rename is closed in the same commit across symbols.txt, delinks.txt, the manifest and actor_renames.tsv, and check_rename_ledger is green on the merged tree, so no .data pointer word links as zero. NON-BLOCKING AND NOT RAISED AS FORMAL FINDINGS, because each is a prose nit already disclosed by the verifier and each claim it makes is still true: include/daObjKurumajiku_c.h and src/game/actors/d_a_obj_km1_ukishima.cpp still spell the retired coined name in explanatory comments, and config/converted-baseline.json is not re-banked in this commit, which tiers_ratchet reads as an un-banked gain rather than a loss. The reconstruction is the work of producer session prod-kuruma-0907; the byte pass of 2026-09-07 is byte evidence only and was not substituted for review at any point here; the source judgment above is mine and the verifier's independent review at the same head is a second, separate one.

source_review.summary: Minimal, in-style tooling fix. plan() sets ztvRebase with exactly _apply()'s rewrite condition (a _ZTV relocation from the kept section, externalised or UNDEF, addend >= VTABLE_PREAMBLE; non-RELA and refused shapes return before the test), so ztvRebase is true iff _apply would change an addend. derive() returns the input only when drop, externalise and ztvRebase are all empty; isolate() writes only when the derived bytes differ, the same shape isolate_many already uses. Every refusal is unchanged; plan_many, derive_many, _apply and the deadstrip, externalise, partition and rebias paths are untouched. Comments and docstrings are short and accurate, including the new isolate() precondition that replaces the idempotence claim, which the caller audit and probe confirm (no caller re-isolates; a re-run would take another 8 off a secondary store). Tests compile with the pinned mwccarm like their neighbours and the factory test fails behaviourally at base. Handoff figures reproduced independently. No attribution impact: no src, include or config path changes. Reviewer note: objects cannot distinguish an explicit extern int _ZTV<C>[] spelled &_ZTV<C>[2] from mwcc's implicit UNDEF vptr store, so a lone-function object with that spelling is now rebased too, as objects with droppable content already were; 0 of 7,069 current objects change. One deferred documentation follow-up outside the reserved scope (F1).

issue.body:
# Finish Spiny shadow reconstruction and complete-object ownership

PR #2863 edits the existing, unenrolled Spiny shadow TU. Local repair `3568a524fe60c5dfa2f3d4ff83451a1b3d11515a` replaces the fabricated Render interface and contradictory state-helper declaration with real calls. The producer reports all 34 functions still match and the complete object remains identical. That repair is local; this issue does not assert publication, independent acceptance or promotion.

Next owner: `codex-integrator-0920`, coordinating separately reserved producer and reviewer work.

- Replace the byte-plus-padding matrix field and aggregate overlays with evidenced real fields, checking every shared-header consumer. Reconstruct the remaining raw helper/state views and ordinary member interfaces without changing relocated bytes.
- Establish the production class identity from the ROM's `daTgz_c` RTTI. Preserve the explicit distinction between that identity and the current community-named Spiny shadow.
- Resolve complete-object ownership and destructor order before promotion. Fresh producer measurements retain nine unlicensed emitted outputs and the reversed D1/D0 ordinal pair; a text match alone does not resolve them.
- Preserve every function's attribution and enrollment identity. Keep the TU in `src_tu/` until the source, complete-object, metadata, relocation and full-ROM gates support a production move.

Remaining matrix and source reconstruction is partial (SP2863-03/04). Correctness findings must be repaired rather than deferred, and any claimed compiler limitation requires a reproducible pinned experiment. Require independent acceptance of the exact candidate and current base before merging.

issue.body:
# Finish BookShot shadow interfaces and complete-object ownership

PR #2868 replaces raw member offsets in the existing BookShot/BookShotSpawner/Bookend shadow TU. Independent checks at `47ee06b41539d307052a7af1b1c1e602bb386f6a` reproduce all 31 functions / 6,040 bytes, with no differing or blind words; the complete object is identical to parent `9022c77b3834c5ee77c31b4fb4af587418137d6c`. This establishes the narrow cleanup's byte neutrality, not finished source reconstruction or promotion.

Next owner: `codex-integrator-0920`, coordinating separately reserved producer and reviewer work.

- Replace the 48-byte matrix overlay beginning at `unk_1ec` and the vector overlay over `unk_438/unk_43c/unk_440` with evidenced real fields. Verify every affected header consumer.
- Reconstruct the remaining raw field helpers, mangled-name bridges and address-access macro using actual class interfaces. Measure ordinary Clear, Update, SetPosRelativeToActor and UpdateYoshiEat calls; do not assert that cleaner forms fail without a pinned experiment.
- Resolve complete-object ownership and lifecycle order before promotion. Independent parent/head checks retain 17 unlicensed emitted outputs, missing compiler-only policies for BookShot D2, BookShotSpawner D2 and Vector3 D1, and the two destructor-order exceptions. Both complete TU checks currently exit with failure despite all text functions matching.
- Preserve symbol credits, actual class-identity evidence and enrollment. Keep this an explicit shadow until complete-object, metadata, relocation and full-ROM checks justify production enrollment.

Track BOOK2868-02/03 as remaining reconstruction/ownership work. This issue does not certify unreviewed surrounding contracts, claim that the PR has merged, or turn the validator's `noverify` result into compiler proof. Require independent source acceptance for the exact candidate and current base.

issue.body:
# Finish BookShot shadow interfaces and complete-object ownership

PR #2868 replaces raw member offsets in the existing BookShot/BookShotSpawner/Bookend shadow TU. Independent checks at `47ee06b41539d307052a7af1b1c1e602bb386f6a` reproduce all 31 functions / 6,040 bytes, with no differing or blind words; the complete object is identical to parent `9022c77b3834c5ee77c31b4fb4af587418137d6c`. This establishes the narrow cleanup's byte neutrality, not finished source reconstruction or promotion.

Next owner: `codex-integrator-0920`, coordinating separately reserved producer and reviewer work.

- Replace the 48-byte matrix overlay beginning at `unk_1ec` and the vector overlay over `unk_438/unk_43c/unk_440` with evidenced real fields. Verify every affected header consumer.
- Reconstruct the remaining raw field helpers, mangled-name bridges and address-access macro using actual class interfaces. Measure ordinary Clear, Update, SetPosRelativeToActor and UpdateYoshiEat calls; do not assert that cleaner forms fail without a pinned experiment.
- Resolve complete-object ownership and lifecycle order before promotion. Independent parent/head checks retain 17 unlicensed emitted outputs, missing compiler-only policies for BookShot D2, BookShotSpawner D2 and Vector3 D1, and the two destructor-order exceptions. Both complete TU checks currently exit with failure despite all text functions matching.
- Preserve symbol credits, actual class-identity evidence and enrollment. Keep this an explicit shadow until complete-object, metadata, relocation and full-ROM checks justify production enrollment.

Track BOOK2868-02/03 as remaining reconstruction/ownership work. This issue does not certify unreviewed surrounding contracts, claim that the PR has merged, or turn the validator's `noverify` result into compiler proof. Require independent source acceptance for the exact candidate and current base.

issue.body:
# Finish BookShot shadow interfaces and complete-object ownership

PR #2868 replaces raw member offsets in the existing BookShot/BookShotSpawner/Bookend shadow TU. Independent checks at `47ee06b41539d307052a7af1b1c1e602bb386f6a` reproduce all 31 functions / 6,040 bytes, with no differing or blind words; the complete object is identical to parent `9022c77b3834c5ee77c31b4fb4af587418137d6c`. This establishes the narrow cleanup's byte neutrality, not finished source reconstruction or promotion.

Next owner: `codex-integrator-0920`, coordinating separately reserved producer and reviewer work.

- Replace the 48-byte matrix overlay beginning at `unk_1ec` and the vector overlay over `unk_438/unk_43c/unk_440` with evidenced real fields. Verify every affected header consumer.
- Reconstruct the remaining raw field helpers, mangled-name bridges and address-access macro using actual class interfaces. Measure ordinary Clear, Update, SetPosRelativeToActor and UpdateYoshiEat calls; do not assert that cleaner forms fail without a pinned experiment.
- Resolve complete-object ownership and lifecycle order before promotion. Independent parent/head checks retain 17 unlicensed emitted outputs, missing compiler-only policies for BookShot D2, BookShotSpawner D2 and Vector3 D1, and the two destructor-order exceptions. Both complete TU checks currently exit with failure despite all text functions matching.
- Preserve symbol credits, actual class-identity evidence and enrollment. Keep this an explicit shadow until complete-object, metadata, relocation and full-ROM checks justify production enrollment.

Track BOOK2868-02/03 as remaining reconstruction/ownership work. This issue does not certify unreviewed surrounding contracts, claim that the PR has merged, or turn the validator's `noverify` result into compiler proof. Require independent source acceptance for the exact candidate and current base.

### Full merge validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|

source_review.summary: First genuine source review of ov045/daObjKm2_Ukishima_c; the 2026-09-07 pass is treated as byte evidence only and nothing in it was carried over. Base: I measured git merge-base origin/main 5a642c837 as b0d348e536fb3304b6ab12d88fe95d780cbeb91d and confirmed the task's declared fd55979f074c7ad796e2846328933363315e7f06 is a strict ancestor of it, so the declared value is stale and the measured fork point is used as both tested_base and reviewed_base. The producer's own handoff note records the same b0d348e53 as the base as shipped, which corroborates the measurement independently. VERDICT RESTS ON THIS: the class model is proved twice over by two methods that could each have refuted it. By hand, the emitted vtable differs from its parent daObjUkiyuka_c at exactly four slots, 0, 3, 16 and 17, and the header declares exactly four things, an inline destructor plus CleanupResources and InitResources; the differing set and the declared set coincide with nothing left over on either side, and slots 6 and 9 are the parent's own Behavior and Render, correctly not redeclared. By tool, romdata_check verifies _ZTV19daObjKm2_Ukishima_c at 128 bytes, all 32 slots relocation-resolved against the cartridge, so this is slot identity and not merely slot shape. The 32-slot length is itself consistent with the dBgActor_c line rather than the 31-slot dActor_c line. NAMES: daObjKm2_Ukishima_c is ROM-attested, not coined; ov045 0x02112f14 holds the NUL-terminated '19daObjKm2_Ukishima_c' and the _ZTI record at 0x02112efc points its middle word at exactly that address, while _ZTI+8 at 0x02112f04 holds 0x02109104, which ov002 names _ZTI14daObjUkiyuka_c and which fixes the base. Retiring the coined FloatingFloorBfs is therefore the ruling applied correctly. The five symbols.txt rows were renamed IN PLACE in this same commit with no alias row and no bounding row added, which is what keeps the .data pointer words resolving by name; had the rename landed without the same-commit symbols.txt edit, those words would link as 0 and no byte gate would have seen it, so this was checked directly and the vtable and profile both verify byte-equal. Because tools/match.py wildcards relocated words, no call target was accepted on byte equality: every branch and literal-pool word in the 0x02111b14..0x02111c30 run was resolved by symbol name instead, and all of them, fBase_c::operator new, dBgActor_cC2Ev, the dBgW_KcMbg and Model member destructors, dActor_cD2Ev, Memory::Deallocate and GAME_HEAP_PTR, are what the source says they are. NO FABRICATED SLOT INTERFACE: the hierarchy is real C++ inheritance through daObjUkiyuka_c to dBgActor_c, there is no struct of function pointers cast over this, no offset-cast dispatch, and no m<hex> member anywhere in the reviewed class, which has no fields of its own at all. The base declares both overridden methods as virtual s32 ...() = 0 with return types matching the derived declarations, so these are genuine overrides and not the silent-inherit trap that an undeclared override would produce. The parent's pure slots are literal zero words in the cartridge, which the differential confirms.
